scope.description: Twelve cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; two new cases are added, one that calls the public snapshot() path on a healthy NoSnapshot cluster and one that drives the same drift and leader change as the previous over-compaction probe over the snapshot-capable entry type, compacts the new leader inside its drifted decided index and then re-synchronizes the replica whose reported accepted index is below the resulting compacted index, with a replica at or above it as control.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot for the healthy control; the snapshot-capable case uses SnapEntry with SnapState (use_snapshots() true, snapshot records the ids of its input entries), the same type the snapshot child investigation already exercised.
The healthy control calls snapshot(Some(decided_idx), true) on the leader of a cluster that has decided five entries plus its StopSign and has never been re-synchronized.

For the snapshot-capable case, three rounds of node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) reproduce the drift, node1.try_become_leader() makes node 1 the leader, and the snapshot is requested with the leader's own decided index as the bound and local_only = true.

reconnected(pid) is always called with the current leader; every drain and every sample runs inside catch_unwind, so a panic inside a handler or a storage call becomes an event field instead of aborting the run.
excluded: No forwarded compaction message is produced, because the snapshot is requested with local_only = true and both cases use one entry type per cluster.
No load, timer, message loss, restart or persistence is exercised.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

parameters.compaction_bound: the leader's own decided index at the time of the call

basis.prefix: Two new cases. The healthy control uses the lineage prefix (node 3 leads, five entries decided, StopSign decided) with the default NoSnapshot entry type, samples all three nodes as SNAPCONTROL_BASE, reads the leader's decided index, calls node3.snapshot(Some(decided), true) inside catch_unwind, emits SNAPCONTROL_SNAP with the decided bound, the panicked flag, the compacted, accepted and decided indexes, then samples SNAPCONTROL_AFTER and emits SNAPCONTROL_RUN_END. The snapshot-capable case builds the same prefix out of SnapEntry values, emits SNAPROBE_LEADER_ELECTED, SNAPROBE_ENTRIES_DECIDED and SNAPROBE_STOPSIGN_DECIDED, performs three rounds of node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) and samples SNAPROBE_DRIFTED, elects node 1 with try_become_leader() and samples SNAPROBE_AFTER_CHANGE, calls node1.snapshot(Some(decided), true) and emits SNAPROBE_SNAP with the panicked flag, the compacted, accepted and decided indexes and the number of ids in the snapshot reachable at index 0, samples SNAPROBE_AFTER_SNAP, then re-synchronizes node 3 (the replica whose reported accepted index is below the compacted index) and emits SNAPROBE_LAG_RESULT with the panicked flag after sampling SNAPROBE_RESYNC_3_N{pid}, repeats the same for node 2 as the control and emits SNAPROBE_AHEAD_RESULT, and finally emits SNAPROBE_RUN_END.

comparisons.description: A public snapshot() call on a healthy cluster whose entry type uses NoSnapshot completes without panicking, so any panic seen in a drifted state is not a property of the drift.
With the snapshot-capable entry type the same compaction call inside the drifted decided index completes without panicking, so the below-compacted state is reached.
The re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index lies below the compacted index is handled without a panic.
After re-synchronizing below the compacted index the replica still exposes the six decided entries of the configuration rather than a shortened or snapshotted decided log.

Control: the replica whose reported accepted index is at or above the compacted index re-synchronizes without a panic, so any deviation in the other stage is attributable to the below-compacted prefix request.

The snapshot is requested with the leader's own decided index as the bound and local_only = true, so no Compaction message is sent to the peers and the compacted index becomes that decided index (the StopSign is no longer counted as decided in the drifted state, so the bound is not lowered).

reconnected(pid) is called with the current leader, because the library only starts a re-synchronization when the peer named is the leader; every drain and sample runs inside catch_unwind, so a panic inside a handler becomes an event field instead of aborting the run.
excluded: No entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in the new case, so the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is not exercised there.
